assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP turned CMB anisotropy into precision cosmology: acoustic peaks, geometry, baryon and dark-matter densities, reionization and a tight Lambda-CDM parameter set. For a theorist concerned with cosmology and inflation-era physics this is a discovery that supports the field's central model with data, and its lasting impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission and instrument team, Page was central to the instrument design and measurement, and Spergel to the cosmological analysis and interpretation. A three-person split is plausible, but the mission was a large collaboration and COBE (2006) and Planck work overlap conceptually, so the credit boundary is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: the results were confirmed independently by Planck and ground-based CMB experiments, and the interpretation has been stable for over a decade. Recognition is arguably overdue, though the 2006 and 2019 prizes already touched CMB and cosmology.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees WMAP as sufficiently distinct from the COBE prize and from Planck.
Fair division of credit within the WMAP team (e.g. the role of Wilkinson, Kogut, Hinshaw), which I cannot resolve from the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Direct imaging of the black-hole shadow in M87* and Sgr A* is a landmark observational result: it probes strong-field gravity at the horizon scale and confirms the existence of compact horizon-scale objects. As a black-hole theorist I find it very compelling as a discovery rather than a model.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow-imaging idea (with Melia and Agol) and championed the project; Doeleman led the VLBI technical development and the EHT collaboration. Zensus was a key leader of the European contribution, but the prize rules and the very large collaboration make a pair or trio contentious.
assessment.maturity: Results from 2019 (M87*) and 2022 (Sgr A*) have been followed by polarization and multi-epoch confirmations, but the interpretation, model dependence of ring size to mass and spin, and independence of reconstructions are still maturing. Perhaps slightly early.
uncertainties: Large collaboration makes the decisive individuals hard to identify.
Image reconstruction depends on priors and modelling; independent re-analyses have been debated.
Whether the idea originators (not in the supplied names) deserve recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms, reached a fractional accuracy of order 1e-18 and opened new tests of relativity, searches for varying constants and a path to redefining the second. It is a clean, foundational invention with broad fundamental-physics reach.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realized early clocks; Ye brought the clock to the highest precision and coherence and showed many-body and gravitational-redshift applications. A two-person prize is natural and clearly supported by the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups worldwide and used in international comparisons; the technology is mature. Overlap with the 2005 (frequency combs) and 2012 (ion control) prizes is a consideration but not a barrier.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to wait for the redefinition of the second.
Possible need to include other pioneers such as Ye's collaborators or Hall, which the supplied credit does not permit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling between a superconducting qubit and a microwave resonator experimentally accessible, giving the architecture behind modern superconducting quantum processors and quantum measurement. The conceptual clarity and the downstream impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Schoelkopf's group, the Yale theory of Girvin and Blais, and Wallraff's first strong-coupling demonstration were jointly decisive. Selecting Schoelkopf, Wallraff and Girvin is a reasonable trio, but Blais's early theory is a real attribution tension.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and widely reproduced since 2004. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits makes timing and overlap a question, but it concerned a different discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 physics prize and how the committee views the relationship.
Exclusion of Alexandre Blais from a three-person cap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, a field with remarkable breadth. The prediction-and-confirmation pairing is attractive.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the decisive 2018 experiments. The trio is directly supported by the supplied names, with Cao and others being junior experimental contributors who are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have reproduced the main phenomena, yet the pairing mechanism in the superconductivity is still debated and the field is changing quickly. Reasonably mature for the discovery, but perhaps early.
uncertainties: Unresolved mechanism of superconductivity.
Sample-dependence and reproducibility across devices.
Credit to early experimentalists not in the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The double pulsar PSR J0737-3039A/B gave the most stringent tests of general relativity in the strong-field regime, with several independent post-Keplerian parameters and a measurement of the Shapiro delay and relativistic spin precession. This is a clean observational result of lasting value to gravity.
assessment.attribution: Burgay discovered the system, Lyne led the Jodrell Bank group and the follow-up, and Kramer led the long-term timing and the tests of GR. The three names map well onto distinct contributions.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: more than twenty years of timing, with all tests still consistent with GR. The Hulse-Taylor prize (1993) is a precedent which may reduce the perceived novelty.
uncertainties: Novelty relative to the 1993 prize.
Role of the other discoverers in the Parkes team, whom I cannot assess from the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane opened neutrino astronomy as a new window on the universe. It is a clear case of a discovery with major lasting consequences.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Spiering was a key figure in building the experiment, but the discovery is the product of a collaboration of hundreds, and early pioneers (AMANDA, Baikal) complicate attribution.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is robust; source identification is still limited to a few objects and the origin of most neutrinos is unresolved. Recognition may be somewhat early, though the discovery is secure.
uncertainties: Source identification remains partial.
Fair credit among IceCube, ANTARES and Baikal pioneers.
Concern about attributing a collaboration discovery to two individuals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The AdS/CFT correspondence is the most influential idea in modern quantum gravity and string theory, with major applications in black-hole information, strongly coupled matter and field theory. Its originality and conceptual influence are undeniable.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena's 1997 paper is the decisive origin; Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten gave the dictionary, while 't Hooft and Susskind provided the holographic principle. I would propose Maldacena alone as the most defensible single configuration, accepting that this is contentious.
assessment.maturity: As a string theorist I note that the duality has no direct empirical confirmation in our universe; support is mathematical and from consistency checks and applications. Whether it is a 'discovery' in the Nobel sense is debatable, so I rank it low in this opening ballot.
uncertainties: No direct experimental test; its status as a physical discovery is uncertain.
Credit would be disputed among several theorists, and the supplied names do not include Gubser or Klebanov.
The committee tradition favors empirically confirmed results.
